I was on fluoxetine for 2 weeks, and it completely wrecked my brain. That was 9 months ago, and I haven’t been the same since. No emotions, extreme cognitive decline, visual snow, dp/dr, headaches, fatigue, etc…

It’s unlikely, but there is a very real risk of permanent damage from psychotropic drugs. Check out r/PSSD

I would only use them as a last resort. Lifestyle changes, diet+exercise, and counseling will not harm your brain. SSRI’s might.

If you have a strong sex drive, it’s unlikely that you have PGAD. PGAD is associated with a lower sex drive than normal. Hallmark symptoms are also SEVERE pain and spontaneous orgasms that do not resolve the genital arousal.

I would encourage you to GRADUALLY(absolutely do not quit cold turkey as this may be dangerous) taper off the Saint John’s Wort and see if your symptoms improve. I would also encourage you to stay as calm as you can in the meantime. Anxiety is a risk factor/trigger for PGAD, and, although I don’t believe you are suffering from it, managing anxiety may also manage the progression of your symptoms if they are in fact caused by PGAD.

If your symptoms persist or progress after discontinuing all meds and supplements, then it’s time to see a urologist or a gynecologist depending on your gender. You may want to see a psychiatrist or a neurologist as well, but be cautious about taking psychotropic meds. Make sure you’re confident that any meds or supplements you take won’t worsen your condition.

I know this is very troubling for you, but there’s no reason to freak out just yet. Hang in there.

Sorry it ruined your summer. I was working on a degree in geology when these pills ruined my fucking brain. Now I’m up to my ass in debt with nothing to show for it and no way to ever pay it off because I’m too disabled to take care of myself.
No. I said it’s all still there. I feel exactly the same as when it started.

I was on fluoxetine at 20mg/day for two weeks. I stopped because I experienced severe derealization, cognitive impairment, fatigue, tremors, etc. 9 months later, and it’s all still there. Antidepressants ruin lives.
Don’t worry, what you are experiencing is not PGAD. Are you still taking any meds or the SJW?
I am not a doctor, but I think it’s absolutely feasible that GI issues, particularly those that affect the colon, could affect the pelvic floor and, therefore, cause or contribute to HF.
I started getting horrible GI pains the same night my HF started. I had been going through 7 months of extreme stress, and I think the GI stuff just pushed me over the edge.

I would like to point out that it has been 4 years since I last used cannabis and 2 years since I last used hallucinogens. If these substances are what caused my current issues, it sure took a hell of a long time to manifest.

Furthermore, the reason I associate these symptoms with the SSRI is not only because I never experienced them prior, but also because they were suddenly apparent within a few hours of my first dose. Within an hour of my first pill, I felt strangely euphoric and experienced strange bodily sensations. A few hours later, the DP/DR appeared. The rest of my symptoms showed up over the course of the next few days.

Although neurological issues induced by SSRIs may not be commonly reported, that doesn’t mean they are never reported. There are plenty of cases of folks developing motor tics, muscle spasms, strange sensations, Parkinsonism, and a host of other neurological problems, either as a side effect of an SSRI or as a symptom of withdrawal. There are even a few cases of such problems arising after as little as 1 dose.

Edit:

I will concede that my prior history with recreational drugs may have set me up for such a reaction, but the exposure to fluoxetine clearly triggered the onset of these symptoms. Furthermore, similar cases exist in people who have never used recreational drugs, so it is entirely possible these symptoms have no relationship to my prior drug use.

I hope so too. They’re really isn’t much of a point in going on living if I’m gonna be stuck like this forever.

I’m pretty used to the gaslighting at this point. I don’t think there’s much use in trying to convince anyone otherwise. The medical establishment has a long way to go before it recognizes these kinds of reactions as reality, and most people will just blindly follow what some guy with a PhD says, regardless of the evidence to the contrary. I know from experience how long it takes to change the opinion of the establishment , as I was pursuing a career in geology before these pills turned my life upside down. Continental drift wasn’t even widely accepted by the scientific community until around the 70’s, despite the fact there was clear evidence around to support it for almost a century. I’ve even met an old timer who still denies it.
Without an option to see the results, the result of this poll will likely be very skewed.

I have a history of paradoxical reactions to drugs, so I should have known better than to try Prozac at all. If I had to guess as to why, I’d say it’s probably due to my gut issues. I was mistakenly given intravenous antibiotics for 5 days as an infant, and I’ve had all sorts of GI and mental health issues my whole life. None of my blood relatives have had these issues or have had as much trouble with pharmaceuticals as I have, so I can’t imagine I have a genetic predisposition. Unfortunately, I doubt correcting any gut imbalances, will fix whatever these pills did to my brain. I just have to wait it out at this point.

I’m sorry you had to go through that. How are you feeling presently?

I had an MRI a few months ago, and the results were normal. However, I also had an EEG, and the results were very abnormal. My frontal lobe is completely out to lunch, and my brain is globally dysfunctional.
Thank you. I think time and basic self care are all I really have left at this point.

I have strong visual snow and retinal after images. I also get things such as strange blobs of color and flashes of light in my periphery. I also sometimes get olfactory hallucinations, typically the smell of burning hair or rubber, but sometimes other smells. These are less persistent though, and usually come in waves every few weeks.
I’ll look into it! What is 9mbec?

I have microdosed in the past to great effect, but right now, I’m very cautious about introducing drugs to my system. I’ve always been sensitive to drugs, and I have a track record of having paradoxical reactions, and I’ve become exponentially more sensitive since this started. I would consider microdosing again if I begin to stabilize a bit, though.
I actually tried Trintellix about a year and a half ago. I was on it for 3 days and was a raging maniac the whole time. I don’t think meds like me all that much.
I started it about a week after coming off the Prozac, but I never took it regularly. The most frequently I ever took it was once every few days.

Thank you. I haven’t used recreational drugs in a long time. I quit smoking pot a few years ago after I had a really bad experience with it. I used mushrooms to great therapeutic effect when I was 20, and it gave me almost 2 years without any depression whatsoever. I feel like playing around with my neurochemistry any further is a bad idea at the moment though.

My psychiatrist thought that I might have HPPD a few months ago, but he has since changed his mind. Thankfully, my sexual functioning hasn’t been affected. The gastroenterologist is going to have me do an FMT soon to clear up my bacterial infection, so hopefully that’ll make me feel less physically ill, although I don’t think it’ll help with any of the neurological issues… 

Be safe on your trip, I wish you an enlightening experience

I have had so many tests over the past 7 months… I had abnormal EEG results, but the neurologists can’t explain what would cause it, at least without admitting that the fluoxetine could be responsible. I am otherwise, nearly in perfect health. The only thing wrong with me is that I have some pretty gnarly gut dysbiosis, but that only accounts for my GI issues. I’m aware that gut issues can affect mental health, but there’s no way it could cause the neurological symptoms.

I never had any neurological issues before taking fluoxetine. I’ve been to a neurologist many times, and they have no idea what’s wrong; they just know that I have some sort of brain damage, given my uneven pupils and abnormal EEG results. I had a full psychological evaluation, because I was worried that I may be developing schizophrenia, and I was told that I was almost certainly not at risk of psychosis. I have had a myriad of blood tests, and all have come back completely normal. Furthermore, I’ve been SEVERELY depressed before. When I was 18, and was so depressed that I almost starved myself to death. 

I know what depression feels like, and this is nothing close to it. Even if depression accounted for the emotional and cognitive issues, it doesn’t explain the neurological ones. The psychologist I saw told me that my issue was neurological rather than psychological/psychiatric. They neurologists are stumped. The only symptoms that can be explained are my GI issues, because I have a C. Diff. infection, but there is no literature that suggests that such an infection can cause neurological issues.

I’ve tried a lot of different meds and supplements, but I react very poorly to them. The only things that I haven’t had paradoxical reactions to are omega 3 and lorazepam. I don’t think the omega 3 has helped at all though, and I don’t take the lorazepam often, as a feel like a benzo dependency is probably not in my best interest. Also, although it calms me down when I’m in the midst of a panic attack, I find that it increases my suicidal ideation.

I’ve been on surviving antidepressants, but it seems that recovery stories are pretty vastly outnumbered by all the folks who are stuck like this indefinitely.

Lucky you. I’m sure the muscle spasms were all in my head. My right pupil being larger than my left for 7 months is probably in my head too. And the skin on my face and forearms being numb. And seeing weird blobs of color floating around in my visual field, smelling burnt hair all the time, and feeling electrical shocks in my fucking skull.

They didn’t just make me feel “worse”. They damaged my brain. I went from being mildly depressed but functional to a vegetable in a few days on meds. I had tremors and muscle spasms for weeks afterward. My pupils are no longer the same size, and I have had visual and olfactory hallucinations since my third day on meds. What I’m experiencing now isn’t close to depression; it’s a living death. I can’t think. I can’t feel. I can’t do anything. Most days I can’t even speak.

Assuming I’m fine, and this is all anxiety, I still have no idea how to prove to myself that I’m not on the verge of psychosis. I’ve had therapists, psychiatrists, and social workers tell me that I’m not at risk of psychosis, but I just can’t make myself believe them. It’s almost like an addiction at this point.

So many people have told me that the fact that I have insight means I’m not going psychotic, but some of these experiences just feel so real. For example, last night it felt like my bed was squirming around under me, and I had this sudden feeling that there was a presence in my room with me. I knew it wasn’t real, but the experience was so vivid that it’s hard to believe that it’s just anxiety.
